 Wisconsin veterans push for Veterans Day to become a paid state holiday 
 Even though it's a federal holiday, Veterans Day is not one of Wisconsin's regular paid state holidays. By Kayla See Published : Nov. 11, 2026 at 9:49 PM CST | Updated : 14 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google MADISON, Wis. (WMTV) - As communities across Wisconsin honored veterans Wednesday, some who served their country called for Veterans Day to become a regular paid holiday for state employees. 
 Although Wisconsin recognizes Veterans Day, November 11 is not one of the state’s nine regular paid holidays for state employees.
 Gov. Tony Evers proposed changing that in his 2025-27 state budget. However, according to the Wisconsin Department of Veterans Affairs website, “Republicans on the state’s budget committee voted to eliminate several provisions from the governor’s proposed budget that would have made Veterans Day a state holiday.”
 Will Jackson, who served in the Marine Corps for eight and a half years, including a deployment to Afghanistan, took the day off work to attend a Veterans Day ceremony at the Wisconsin State Capitol.
 “It could be something that legislation should work on,” Jackson said. “I believe wholeheartedly that every veteran is absolutely important to the fabric of our country.”
 Mary Parker, a member of the Daughters of the American Revolution and the State Chair of America250, also attended the ceremony. 
 Her father served in the military for 30 years, including three tours in Vietnam, before passing away in April.
 “I wish they would make it a legal state holiday,” Parker said. “It’s good that we have time to come together because of this event, but it would be nice if it would be a state holiday.”
 Wisconsin state employees receive an additional personal holiday in recognition of Veterans Day, which they can use at their discretion. 
 However, November 11 is not automatically a paid day off.
 For Jackson, the day is about more than time away from work. It is an opportunity to recognize those who served and the sacrifices they made.
 “Veterans Day, for me personally, is a time to remember the sacrifice of so many,” Jackson said.
